chapter: String bands, serenading and violin players
title: What bands were paid for dances and clubs in the early days
summary: String bands rarely played dances; dance hosts hired seven- or eight-piece bands for around three dollars to three-fifty a man at clubs like the Autocrat.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did you use it to play dancing with a band like that too?

Well, we, uh, we could play it, you know, but it wasn't too much, you know. Most of the dancing people would hire bands. Music was so cheap at that time, you could get a band for three dollars and a half a man. Three dollars a man. Yeah. About seven or eight piece bands could play, you know, like, like the, uh, the Autocrat Club.
Yeah. Franz O'Veir, Santa's Senna's, all them clubs. You, uh, you could take eight, nine piece bands in there and make good music and they'd have big dances there.
